example_summary: Computes the tax liability for Mr. Manish (age 47) under the Old Tax Regime, demonstrating the application of the ₹ 2,50,000 basic exemption and the Section 87A rebate for a total income of ₹ 4,15,000.
source_provision:
| Total Income Range | Applicable Tax Rate (Old Regime: < 60 Years) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Up to ₹ 2,50,000 | **Nil** (Basic Exemption Limit) |
| ₹ 2,50,001 to ₹ 5,00,000 | **5%** of income exceeding ₹ 2,50,000 |
| ₹ 5,00,001 to ₹ 10,00,000 | **₹ 12,500 + 20%** of income exceeding ₹ 5,00,000 |
| Above ₹ 10,00,000 | **₹ 1,12,500 + 30%** of income exceeding ₹ 10,00,000 |


| Provision Aspect | Statutory Rule under Section 87A (Old Tax Regime) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Eligible Assessee** | **Resident Individual** only (Non-residents not eligible) |
| **Total Income Threshold** | Total Income after Chapter VI-A deductions $\le$ **₹ 5,00,000** |
| **Maximum Rebate Amount** | **Lower of 100% of tax liability** or **₹ 12,500** |


**Key Statutory Conditions & Mechanics:**

* **Opt-out Mechanism u/s 115BAC(6):** Assessee must exercise the option to shift out of the default tax regime on or before the due date u/s 139(1) for the relevant Assessment Year.

* **Sequence of Computation:** Tax Liability before Cess $\rightarrow$ Deduct Rebate u/s 87A $\rightarrow$ Apply Health & Education Cess @ 4% on net tax liability.


> [!IMPORTANT] Section 87A Exemption Limit Difference: Under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC), the Rebate u/s 87A threshold is higher (Total Income up to ₹ 7,00,000 with max rebate ₹ 25,000), whereas under the Old Tax Regime, the threshold remains strictly ₹ 5,00,000 with max rebate ₹ 12,500.

director.justification: Computes the step-by-step tax liability under the old regime for a resident individual with income of ₹ 4,15,000, applying basic exemption slab and Section 87A rebate to arrive at Nil tax.
director.visual_metaphor: A step-by-step financial computation ledger balancing income slabs and deducting Section 87A rebate shield to yield zero net liability.
